Subject: Quantified deal sprint: private deployment pricing and next steps

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few targeted asks so we can convert the discovery into an actionable quote: 

Call highlights / assumptions we captured:
- Primary use: clinical summarization + real-time assistant for clinicians (token mix heavily generation-forward).
- Estimated steady-state monthly tokens: 40M–80M generated tokens (plus ~5–10M input tokens).
- Target unit economics goal you mentioned: ~$900–1,100 per 1M generated tokens (targeted blended cost).
- Preferred deployment: Private (VPC hosted in your AWS account) with on-prem option later if needed.

Specific qualification items we need to finalize pricing options (please confirm):
1) Environment count: do you want separate prod + staging + dev (3 envs) or prod + staging only?
2) Support tier: Standard (business hours), Premium (24/7 monitored), Enterprise (named SLA + SRE runbook) — which level maps to your internal expectations?
3) License model preference: (A) annual platform license + committed token throughput, (B) reserved GPU capacity monthly + license, or (C) consumption-only per-token billing for private (higher unit price). Any leanings?
4) Procurement cadence: target PO / contract date you are aiming for? (you mentioned Q3 earlier — is that commit or evaluation?)

What we'll send next (by tomorrow):
- 2 pricing pathways (license + committed tokens vs reserved capacity) with example math to reach your $/1M target, and hit the environment/support combos you choose. (attached: private_pricing_scenarios.xlsx)
- A short mutual action plan (MAP) that maps milestones, deliverables, security checklist, and procurement steps (attached: mutual_action_plan_draft.pdf).

Next steps: can you confirm answers to the 4 qualification items above? Also availability for a 30-min follow-up on Mon 26 Apr or Tue 27 Apr for a walkthrough of the pricing scenarios.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman

Hi Aisha — appreciate the recap, that matches my notes. Answers inline below: 

1) Environment count: We need 3 envs (prod, pre-prod/staging, dev). Production must be isolated from dev.
2) Support tier: Enterprise — we need 24/7 escalation and a named technical lead during onboarding.
3) License model: We prefer an annual committed model (option A) if the unit economics get us under ~$1,000 per 1M generated tokens. If not, show us the reserved GPU path and cost delta.
4) Procurement cadence: Target is to complete evaluation and have contract signed in early Aug (so Q3 commit). Procurement will need a clear SOW, SOC2 evidence, and a bollus on pricing for year 1 vs year 2.

Budget context: For an initial year-1 deployment across 3 envs we are eyeing a budget range ~$150k–250k (platform + support + reserved capacity), but that number is flexible if unit economics skew favorably.

I can do Mon 26 Apr 10:00am PT for a pricing walkthrough.

Thanks — Sam

Thanks Sam — helpful clarity. A couple of quick notes from pricing/solutions perspective and what we'll model for Monday's walkthrough: 

Pricing constructs we'll present (high-level):
- Path A (Committed annual license + committed token band): fixed platform fee (annually) + guaranteed token band with stepped discounting. Example: $80k license + discounted tokens to hit ~$850–950 per 1M with a 12-month 60M commit.
- Path B (Reserved GPU slab + platform license): platform fee + reserved GPU pool sized for your p95 throughput; staggered environments (shared staging/dev) could reduce incremental GPU cost. This tends to hit lower per-token for heavy generation bursts.
- Path C (Consumption private): no commit license (higher unit price), simpler procurement but ~25–40% premium vs committed.

Items we'll need from your side before we finalize an accurate quote (please DM or drop in the shared Drive):
- Expected peak QPS / concurrency for production (gives us GPU slab sizing).
- Any hard constraint on data residency or on-prem requirement beyond VPC in your AWS account.
- PO template (if you have standard procurement terms) and suggested SLA language if you want to modify our defaults.

I'll bring an initial model that converts your indicated 40M–80M generated tokens into two year-1 pricing outcomes (conservative and aggressive adoption curves), showing blended $/1M and net ARR. Aisha — attaching the recommended scenarios (private_pricing_scenarios.xlsx) + draft MAP for procurement.

Agenda for Mon 26 Apr 10:00am PT walkthrough:
1) Review the two scenarios and assumptions (10 min)
2) Model sensitivity: unit econ vs commit level (10 min)
3) Procurement milestones & SOC2 / security checklist (5 min)
4) Next steps and immediate follow-ups (5 min)

If that looks good, we'll update the MAP to include procurement contacts and dates.

— Karthik
